page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance in the ecs.g8ae instance family running under the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical AMD EPYC 9T34 cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture includes an x86_64 instruction set supporting AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, SHA, and FMA vector instructions. Cache sizing measures 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage and standard host resources while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC 9T34 processor yields top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng tests and strong single-core and multi-core results in Geekbench. PassMark testing highlights strong memory throughput and hardware-accelerated encryption capabilities. Multi-core compute performance across stress-ng, PassMark CPU tests, and software compilation tasks lands in the middle benchmark tier. The absence of integrated ephemeral SSD storage requires external block storage attachment for persistent data, which influences overall I/O latency profiles. However, high single-threaded clock performance combined with AVX-512 vector support enables efficient processing of vectorized workloads and web traffic.

From a hardware density perspective, the balanced 1:4 memory allocation paired with 20 Gbps network connectivity offers predictable compute efficiency for medium-to-large scalable enterprise services. Suitable workloads include enterprise web application serving, Redis caching nodes, API gateways, software compilation environments, and general-purpose database hosts utilizing attached block storage.
